ei.title: Chapter 5-14 Analysis: Why Bystanders Don't Intervene
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting (A)[normally / abnormally] when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us (B)[uncomfortable / comfortable]. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that (C)[enable / prevent] them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 방관자는 반응하지 않을 때 '정상적으로(normally)' 행동하는 것이며, 그 통찰은 우리를 '불편하게(uncomfortable)' 만들고, 문제는 그들이 돕는 것을 '막는(prevent)' 성격적 결함에서 비롯되지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① normally — uncomfortable — prevent — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② abnormally — uncomfortable — prevent (A 반대: 정상적으로→비정상적으로)
❌ ③ normally — comfortable — prevent (B 반대: 불편한→편안한)
❌ ④ normally — uncomfortable — enable (C 반대: 막다→가능하게 하다)
det.tip: prevent A from -ing = A가 ~하는 것을 막다

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in (A)[constrains / frees] their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting (B)[weaker / stronger]. No one bystander feels enough (C)[collective / personal] responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 상황이 방관자의 행동을 '제약하며(constrains)', 책임이 흩어져 '더 약해지고(weaker)', 누구도 반응할 만큼의 '개인적(personal)' 책임을 느끼지 못한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① frees — weaker — personal (A 반대: 제약하다→풀어주다)
✅ ② constrains — weaker — personal — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ constrains — stronger — personal (B 반대: 더 약한→더 강한)
❌ ④ constrains — weaker — collective (C 반대: 개인적인→집단적인)

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we (A)[realize / overlook]. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders (B)[witness / ignore] an emergency, responsibility apparently (C)[concentrates / diffuses] among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 상황은 우리가 '깨닫는(realize)' 것보다 행동을 더 제약하며, 여러 방관자가 응급 상황을 '목격할(witness)' 때 책임이 그들 사이로 '흩어진다(diffuses)'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① overlook — witness — diffuses (A 반대: 깨닫다→간과하다)
❌ ② realize — ignore — diffuses (B 반대: 목격하다→무시하다)
✅ ③ realize — witness — diffuses — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ realize — witness — concentrates (C 반대: 흩어지다→집중되다)

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting ①<u>normally</u> when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that ②<u>prevent</u> them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in ③<u>constrains</u> their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting ④<u>stronger</u>. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 책임이 방관자들 사이로 흩어지면 '더 약해져야(weaker)' 하는데 '더 강해진다(stronger)'는 것은 문맥상 반대이다.
det.analysis:
① normally — 정상적으로, 원문 일치
② prevent — 막다, 원문 일치
③ constrains — 제약하다, 원문 일치
④ stronger — 원문은 weaker(더 약한) ←정답
det.tip: 책임 분산 → 각자가 느끼는 책임은 weaker(약해짐)

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us ①<u>comfortable</u>. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will ②<u>intervene</u>. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders ③<u>witness</u> an emergency, responsibility apparently ④<u>diffuses</u> among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 우리도 똑같이 반응하지 못할 것이라는 통찰은 우리를 '불편하게(uncomfortable)' 만든다. '편안하게(comfortable)'는 문맥상 반대이다.
det.analysis:
① comfortable — 원문은 uncomfortable(불편한) ←정답
② intervene — 개입하다, 원문 일치
③ witness — 목격하다, 원문 일치
④ diffuses — 흩어지다, 원문 일치
det.tip: insight makes us uncomfortable = 그 통찰이 우리를 불편하게 만든다

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological ①<u>insight</u> makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we ②<u>realize</u>. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will ③<u>withdraw</u>. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough ④<u>personal</u> responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 방관자가 많을수록 누구든 한 명이 '개입할(intervene)' 가능성이 더 낮아진다는 것이 방관자 효과이다. '물러날(withdraw)'은 문맥상 반대이다.
det.analysis:
① insight — 통찰, 원문 일치
② realize — 깨닫다, 원문 일치
③ withdraw — 원문은 intervene(개입하다) ←정답
④ personal — 개인적인, 원문 일치
det.tip: the less likely ~ will intervene = 개입할 가능성이 더 낮다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 방관자가 많을수록 그들 중 누구든 한 명이 '개입할' 가능성이 더 낮아진다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① hesitate — 망설이다 (개입할 가능성이 아니라 반대 뉘앙스)
❌ ② celebrate — 축하하다 (문맥 무관)
✅ ③ intervene — 개입하다, 끼어들다 ←정답
❌ ④ disappear — 사라지다 (문맥 무관)

det.korean: 여러 방관자가 응급 상황을 목격하면, 책임이 그들 사이로 '흩어져' 점점 약해진다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① concentrates — 집중되다 (약해진다는 뒤 내용과 모순)
❌ ② strengthens — 강화되다 (getting weaker와 모순)
❌ ③ multiplies — 배가되다 (문맥 반대)
✅ ④ diffuses — 흩어지다, 확산되다 ←정답
det.tip: diffuse + getting weaker = 흩어져서 약해진다 (책임 분산)

det.korean: 방관자가 처한 상황이 우리가 깨닫는 것보다 그들의 행동을 더 '제약한다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① constrains — 제약하다, 억제하다 ←정답
❌ ② frees — 풀어주다 (반대 의미)
❌ ③ describes — 묘사하다 (문맥 무관)
❌ ④ ignores — 무시하다 (상황이 행동을 무시한다는 것은 어색)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 usually의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: usually = 대개, 보통 → generally
det.analysis:
❌ ① rarely — 드물게 (반의어)
✅ ② generally — 일반적으로, 대개 ←정답
❌ ③ briefly — 잠깐 (의미축 다름: 시간)
❌ ④ hardly — 거의 ~않다 (반대 뉘앙스)

det.korean: constrains = 제약하다 → restricts
det.analysis:
❌ ① frees — 풀어주다 (반의어)
❌ ② reveals — 드러내다 (의미축 다름)
✅ ③ restricts — 제한하다, 억제하다 ←정답
❌ ④ delays — 지연시키다 (의미축 다름: 시간)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 witness의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: witness = (사건을) 목격하다 → observe
det.analysis:
❌ ① cause — 야기하다 (의미축 다름)
❌ ② avoid — 피하다 (반대 뉘앙스)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 weaker의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: weaker(더 약한) ↔ stronger(더 강한)
det.analysis:
✅ ① stronger — 더 강한 (반의어) ←정답
❌ ② quieter — 더 조용한 (의미축 다름: 소리)
❌ ③ larger — 더 큰 (의미축 다름: 크기)
❌ ④ closer — 더 가까운 (의미축 다름: 거리)

det.korean: prevent(막다, 못하게 하다) ↔ allow(허용하다, ~하게 두다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① delay — 지연시키다 (의미축 다름: 시간을 늦출 뿐 막지 않음)

questions.passage:
(A) The problem with bystanders does not <u>stem</u> from defects in their character.

(B) She carefully cut the <u>stem</u> of the rose before placing it in the vase.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 stem의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) stem from ~ = ~에서 기인하다/비롯되다 (동사) / (B) stem = (식물의) 줄기 (명사)
det.analysis:
❌ ① 줄기 — 기인하다 (A와 B의 의미가 뒤바뀜)
❌ ② 막다 — 줄기 (A는 '막다'가 아니라 '기인하다')
✅ ③ 기인하다 — 줄기 ←정답
❌ ④ 기인하다 — 잎 (B는 '잎'이 아니라 '줄기')
det.tip: stem from = ~에서 비롯되다 (원인) vs stem = 줄기 (식물)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"a serious, unexpected, and often dangerous situation that requires immediate action"

det.korean: 즉각적인 행동이 필요한 심각하고 예기치 못한 위험한 상황 → emergency
det.analysis:
❌ ① insight — 통찰 (상황이 아님)
❌ ② character — 성격, 성품 (상황이 아님)
❌ ③ behavior — 행동 (상황이 아님)
✅ ④ emergency — 응급 상황, 비상 사태 ←정답
det.tip: emergency = 즉각 대응이 필요한 비상 상황

questions.passage: That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave __________ (different), better.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 동사 behave(행동하다)를 꾸미는 자리 → 부사가 필요 → different(형용사) → differently(부사)
det.analysis: behave __________ 는 동사 뒤에서 '어떻게 행동하는지'를 꾸미는 부사 자리예요. 그래서 형용사 different를 부사 differently로 바꿔요.

questions.passage: But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, __________ (responsible) apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 동사 diffuses의 주어 자리이므로 명사가 필요 → responsible(형용사) → responsibility(명사)
det.analysis: 빈칸은 뒤의 동사 diffuses(흩어진다)의 주어예요. 주어 자리에는 명사가 와야 하므로, 형용사 responsible을 명사 responsibility로 바꿔요.

But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough __________ to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 책임이 분산되면, 어느 방관자도 반응할 만큼 충분한 '개인적 책임'을 느끼지 못한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① social pressure — 사회적 압박 (책임 분산의 결과는 압박이 아니라 책임 결여)
✅ ② personal responsibility — 개인적 책임 ←정답
❌ ③ public attention — 대중의 관심 (문맥 무관)
❌ ④ emotional distance — 정서적 거리 (문맥 무관)
det.tip: 책임 분산 → 개인이 느끼는 personal responsibility가 줄어든다

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, __________. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 책임이 방관자들 사이로 흩어지면서(diffuses) 점점 '약해진다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① getting weaker — 점점 약해지는 ←정답
❌ ② growing stronger — 더 강해지는 (뒤에 누구도 책임을 못 느낀다는 내용과 모순)
❌ ③ becoming urgent — 긴급해지는 (문맥 무관)
❌ ④ acting quickly — 빠르게 행동하는 (책임은 행동의 주어가 아님)
det.tip: diffuse(흩어지다) → 각자가 느끼는 책임은 getting weaker(약해짐)
